equalTensionInference.kind: explicit mechanics inference from ideal-pulley model and primary strand rule
equalTensionInference.independentJudgment: IMA omits friction; each load-bearing branch counts, including a branch that also redirects. In the conventional ideal continuous massless rope and frictionless pulley model, tangential torque balance at every free pulley gives equal tension on its two sides; otherwise a massless free pulley would have nonzero net torque. With n parallel supporting branches the supporting force is nT; a redirect-only branch contributes no force to the moving load. This verifies equal tension and branch counting as physical inference, not a sentence quoted from Yale. Parallelism alone is not the cause of equal tension. Separate independently tensioned ropes or accelerated massive pulleys are outside this elementary ideal-pulley model.
